decision.statement: Which rolling-resistance projection of the round-2 grain-shape surrogate mu_r is admissible: (i) keep the TensorDEM lever convention (lever = particle radius r for pair and wall) and quote mu_r only inside TensorDEM, (ii) adopt the LIGGGHTS EPSD2 reduced-radius convention (reff = r for wall, radi*radj/(radi+radj) = r/2 for equal spheres) as the default, or (iii) add (ii) as an opt-in switch plus a published parameter-mapping factor.
decision.adopt_rule: Adopt an OSS convention as the *default* only if the TensorDEM law deviates from the OSS law by more than 15% on a closed single-contact metric with an analytic reference AND the port keeps the energy ledger. Otherwise keep the legacy default and publish the mapping factor.

hypotheses.H1: The TensorDEM rolling law is a different *family* from the OSS rolling models (elastic-plastic spring vs constant directional torque), so trajectories disagree by more than 15%.
hypotheses.H2: The two codes implement the same family (linear rolling spring + Coulomb cap) and differ only in the lever arm reff and in torsion handling.
hypotheses.H3: A literature/OSS value of mu_r is transferable between codes without a conversion factor.

metrics.M1_t_stop: rolling spin-down stopping time of one sphere on a plane (closed-form reference (5/7) mu_r g)
metrics.M2_t_half_pair: half-time of the relative-spin relaxation of an equal-sphere pair (reference: Coulomb-saturated linear decay)
metrics.M3_creep: residual speed of a sphere on a slope below/above arctan(mu_r)
metrics.M5_dt: fraction of the OSS Rayleigh timestep used by the case timestep
metrics.M6_identity: max |omega_kernel - omega_OSS| on a wall-contact spin-down (identity check)

baseline_control.analytic: M1, M2, M3 thresholds derived in the docstring of tensordem.xval.scenes (not fitted)
baseline_control.oss_reference: LIGGGHTS-PUBLIC @3d5c00f2, rolling_model_cdt.h / rolling_model_epsd2.h / fix_check_timestep_gran.cpp, transcribed in tensordem.xval.oss_rolling
baseline_control.negative_control: legacy TensorDEM law with reff = r (the current default) on the same scenes; a null result there means 'no port needed'

stopping_rule: Run every sweep point once (deterministic scenes, no stochastic sampling); no point is dropped. A metric that lands inside +/-15% of the reference supports the mapping arm; outside, the difference is reported as a law difference.
exclusions: No thermal, cohesive or non-spherical contacts; single-contact scenes only. The macroscopic column-level arms (benchmarks/xval_dem_round2_column_arms.py) were not executed in this round (compute budget) - declared as an open item.
interpretation_limits: The OSS reference is a *source transcription*, not a compiled LIGGGHTS binary: identical formulas, but no cross-code integration test.
The Hertz-equivalent shear modulus used in M5 is a declared mapping (one grain weight on the case's linear kn), not a material property.
Creep speeds below the static threshold are dt- and hysteresis-dependent in both laws; they are reported, not used as pass/fail.
